oewn-00307252-n.learner: the act of going from one place to another
examples: It was a journey of only twenty-four miles, and they began it so early as to be in Gracechurch Street by noon.
The coach, therefore, took them the first stage of their journey, and brought its master back to Longbourn.
Who should suffer but myself?
Nobody can tell what I suffer!

oewn-02113644-v.learner: to go through something, or to have something done to you
examples: Mr. Bingley, if he had been imposed on, would have much to suffer when the affair became public.

oewn-00670017-v.learner: to put up with something or someone that is unpleasant
examples: She would not suffer such rudeness at her own table.
Observing his second daughter employed in trimming a hat, he suddenly addressed her
he addressed the mother in these words

oewn-00992687-v.learner: to go up to someone and speak to them
examples: A stranger addressed me in the street and asked the way to the station.

oewn-01163215-v.learner: to turn yourself and your effort to something, such as a question
examples: She addressed herself to the task of clearing the table.

oewn-00899241-v.learner: to put a question to someone and expect them to answer
examples: I inquired after their brother, of course.
He was then, he said, on his way to Longbourn on purpose to inquire after her.

oewn-00787624-v.learner: to look into something carefully in order to find out the facts about it
examples: She then proceeded to inquire into the measures which her father had intended to pursue

oewn-00159090-r.learner: with no other person there and nothing else there

oewn-00009062-r.learner: with no others counted in or taking part
examples: He spoke of it as a certain event, of which the time alone could be undecided.

oewn-00049277-r.learner: at once, without waiting or hesitating, with no time passing in between
examples: The express was sent off directly.

oewn-00506737-r.learner: with no person and no thing coming in between
examples: She heard the news directly from her uncle, and not from a servant.

oewn-00052386-r.learner: in a straight line, without turning aside
examples: The lane runs directly to the church door.

oewn-00023451-n.learner: what the mind ends up holding after noticing things, learning and thinking
examples: Every day added something to their knowledge of the officers' names and connections.

oewn-01051260-a.learner: being the second of two people or things that have been named, or the last one or ones of several

To make this latter observation quite exact we must not use the term miniature in its restricted sense

oewn-00122978-v.learner: to become different in some way while still keeping what you or it were before

oewn-00109468-v.learner: to become different in what you really are, so that you are no longer what you were
examples: After those years abroad he had changed entirely, and nothing of the old man was left.
